pharm: Antagonist at dopamine D2, serotonin 5-HT2A and 5-HT7 receptors with partial agonism at 5-HT1A; little or no affinity for histamine H1 or muscarinic M1 receptors.
quick: Schizophrenia: start 40 mg/day (max 160); bipolar depression: start 20 mg/day (max 120)
Must take with food (at least 350 calories)
Third-trimester use risks neonatal EPS/withdrawal; use only if needed
No human milk data; present in rat milk; weigh benefit
Moderate: start 20 mg, max 80 mg/day; severe: max 40 mg/day
Weight, glucose, lipids, EPS, prolactin, CBC, orthostatic BP, mood/suicidality
summary: Lurasidone hydrochloride is an atypical antipsychotic indicated for schizophrenia (adults and adolescents 13-17 years) and for depressive episodes of bipolar I disorder (bipolar depression) as monotherapy in adults and pediatric patients 10-17 years, and as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate in adults. It must be taken with food (at least 350 calories), which substantially increases absorption. It carries a boxed warning that elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotics are at increased risk of death (lurasidone is not approved for dementia-related psychosis), and a boxed warning for increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients. Lurasidone is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and strong CYP3A4 inducers, and requires dose caps in renal and hepatic impairment.
indications: Schizophrenia in adults and adolescents (13 to 17 years)
Depressive episode associated with bipolar I disorder (bipolar depression) in adults and pediatric patients (10 to 17 years) as monotherapy
Depressive episode associated with bipolar I disorder in adults as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate

admin: Take once daily with food (at least 350 calories); food roughly doubles AUC and triples Cmax
No initial dose titration is required for schizophrenia or bipolar depression
Reduce the dose to half when a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is added; increase the dose with a moderate CYP3A4 inducer
Do not use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or strong CYP3A4 inducers, and avoid grapefruit/grapefruit juice
Apply renal and hepatic dose caps as appropriate
moa: The mechanism of lurasidone in schizophrenia and bipolar depression is not fully established but is thought to be mediated through a combination of central dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptor antagonism. It binds with high affinity to D2, 5-HT2A, and 5-HT7 receptors, is a partial agonist at 5-HT1A, and an antagonist at alpha-2 adrenergic receptors, with negligible histamine H1 and muscarinic M1 activity.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to lurasidone or formulation components (angioedema reported)
Concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, voriconazole, mibefradil)
Concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, avasimibe, St. John's wort, phenytoin, carbamazepine)
relative: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning: increased mortality and cerebrovascular events; not approved)
Pediatric and young adult patients (boxed warning: increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors)
History of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, or dyslipidemia
Cardiovascular/cerebrovascular disease, dehydration, or hypovolemia (orthostatic hypotension)
History of seizures or conditions lowering seizure threshold
Pre-existing low WBC or history of leukopenia/neutropenia
Bipolar disorder (risk of activation of mania/hypomania)
monitor: Extrapyramidal symptoms, akathisia, and tardive dyskinesia
CBC in patients with low WBC or prior leukopenia/neutropenia
Orthostatic vital signs; mood and suicidal ideation

preg: Neonates exposed to antipsychotic drugs during the third trimester are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms (agitation, hypertonia, hypotonia, tremor, somnolence, respiratory distress, feeding disorder) after delivery; severity varies and some require prolonged hospitalization. There are no adequate human studies; animal studies showed no teratogenic effects up to 1.5-times (rat) and 6-times (rabbit) the maximum recommended human dose. Use only if needed and monitor neonates.
lact: There are no data on the presence of lurasidone in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or on milk production. Lurasidone is present in rat milk. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need for lurasidone and potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: Patients with moderate (CrCl 30 to <50 mL/min) or severe (CrCl <30 mL/min) renal impairment have higher lurasidone exposure. Reduce the maximum recommended dosage: start at 20 mg/day with a maximum of 80 mg/day.
hepatic: Patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score >=7) have higher exposure. Start at 20 mg/day; the maximum is 80 mg/day in moderate (Child-Pugh 7-9) and 40 mg/day in severe (Child-Pugh 10-15) hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, voriconazole, mibefradil): contraindicated
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, avasimibe, St. John's wort, phenytoin, carbamazepine): contraindicated
moderate: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (diltiazem, atazanavir, erythromycin, fluconazole, verapamil): halve the lurasidone dose
Moderate CYP3A4 inducers (bosentan, efavirenz, etravirine, modafinil, nafcillin): may need to increase the lurasidone dose
Other CNS depressants and alcohol: additive sedation
minor: Lithium and valproate: minimal effect on lurasidone exposure; no adjustment needed
interactions.food: Must be taken with food (at least 350 calories) to ensure adequate absorption; exposure is independent of meal fat content and similar for 350 to 1000 calorie meals.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate prolactin and serum creatinine; can produce metabolic laboratory changes (glucose, lipids).

serious: Increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors (pediatric/young adults)

monitoring: Weight/BMI, fasting glucose, and lipids at baseline and periodically
Extrapyramidal symptoms, akathisia, and tardive dyskinesia
CBC in patients with low WBC or prior leukopenia/neutropenia; discontinue at first sign of significant WBC decline
Orthostatic blood pressure and heart rate, especially at initiation and dose escalation
Mood, clinical worsening, and suicidal ideation, especially early in therapy and at dose changes
counsel: Always take with food (at least 350 calories) - it is not absorbed well on an empty stomach
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice and tell your doctor about all other medicines
May cause drowsiness or dizziness; rise slowly and avoid driving until you know how it affects you; avoid alcohol
Watch for and report new or worsening depression, agitation, or thoughts of self-harm (especially younger patients)
Report abnormal movements, restlessness, high fever with stiffness, fainting, or signs of infection; attend metabolic monitoring visits
pk: Antipsychotic/antidepressant effect over days to weeks; steady state within ~7 days
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions 15-30 C permitted
pearls: Absorption is food-dependent: a meal of at least 350 calories roughly doubles AUC and triples Cmax
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers are absolute contraindications; halve the dose with moderate inhibitors
Generally lower metabolic and weight-gain burden than several other atypical antipsychotics
Renal cap (CrCl <50): start 20 mg, max 80 mg/day; hepatic cap: max 80 mg (moderate) or 40 mg (severe)
Avoid epinephrine/beta-agonists in overdose-related hypotension due to alpha blockade
missed: Take the missed dose with food as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once, and always take with food.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Provide supportive care with close monitoring and consider multiple-drug involvement; consult a poison control center. Begin cardiovascular and continuous ECG monitoring for arrhythmias. Treat hypotension and circulatory collapse with appropriate measures - do NOT use epinephrine, dopamine, or other beta-agonist sympathomimetics, as beta stimulation may worsen hypotension in the setting of lurasidone-induced alpha blockade. Treat severe extrapyramidal symptoms with anticholinergics. Consider gastric lavage (with airway protection) and activated charcoal with a laxative; beware aspiration risk from obtundation, seizures, or dystonic reactions.
